claims.text: Singleton: the container creates the instance the first time it is requested and returns the same instance for the app's lifetime. Scoped: one instance per scope. Transient: a new instance on every resolve.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: Dependency injection in .NET, Service lifetimes

claims.text: In ASP.NET Core, a scope is created per request; scoped services are shared within the request and disposed at the end of the request.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: Service lifetimes (Scoped: in apps that process requests, disposed at the end of the request); ASP.NET Core DI docs

claims.text: EF Core does not support multiple parallel operations on the same DbContext instance; it throws when it detects concurrent use, and otherwise behaviour is undefined (possible wrong results or corruption).
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: DbContext lifetime, configuration and initialization (avoiding DbContext threading issues)

claims.text: AddDbContext registers the context with a scoped lifetime by default.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: DbContext in dependency injection for ASP.NET Core; AddDbContext contextLifetime default Scoped

claims.text: At stage-1, AddDonHangInfrastructure registers DonHangDbContext with AddDbContext and EfOrderRepository and LoggingNotifier with AddScoped; Program.cs registers OrderService with AddScoped and JwtTokenService with AddSingleton.
Within one request, OrdersController and OrderService receive the same EfOrderRepository instance, which holds the same DonHangDbContext, because both are scoped.
JwtTokenService receives IConfiguration, reads the Jwt settings from it inside IssueToken on each call (used at login), and has no mutable fields.

Program.cs creates a scope with app.Services.CreateScope() before migrations, resolves DonHangDbContext from scope.ServiceProvider, and the using block disposes the scope and the scoped context with it.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: DonHang.Api/Program.cs:57-62; .NET docs: IServiceScope disposal disposes scoped services

claims.text: If EfOrderRepository were transient and DonHangDbContext scoped, the controller and OrderService would get two repositories sharing one context within a request.
Lifetime choice affects correctness (who shares an object), not only performance.
